source.title: Increased decision thresholds trigger extended information gathering across the compulsivity spectrum

confidence_rationale: Strong on the claim's FORM and adverse to its CONTENT, which is why it is 'mixed' rather than either pole. It confirms that a single accumulation-threshold parameter generates a dissociable, dimensionally-graded commitment phenotype in a large population-representative sample -- the shape MECH-080 predicts. But it lands extended, over-withheld commitment on the COMPULSIVITY dimension, where MECH-080 assigns extension-bias to anxiety and reserves compulsivity/OCD for attractor lock-in. Held below 0.7 because the accumulation threshold governs an information-sampling stopping rule, not forward-rollout depth.
failure_signatures: Extended information gathering loaded on compulsivity and NOT on the anxiety/depression dimensions measured in the same sample -- MECH-080's arm 2 (anxiety = extension-biased, suppressed commitment) predicts the opposite loading and is not observed here.

The threshold effect was driven by DELAYED EMERGENCE OF URGENCY rather than a statically raised bound, so a REE manipulation that sets a fixed higher commit threshold would not reproduce the mechanism the paper identifies.
If one parameter family is to produce all three of MECH-080's arms, this result forces compulsivity onto the extension arm, leaving arm 3 (lock-in) without a distinct psychiatric occupant.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a population-representative sample stratified by psychiatric dimension, subjects high in compulsivity sampled more information before committing on a sequential information-gathering task; computational modelling attributed this to a raised decision threshold arising from a delayed emergence of an impatience/urgency signal, and the effect was specific to the compulsivity dimension.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct external support for MECH-080's core architectural bet: that a commitment-threshold parameter sitting on top of a sampling/search process is sufficient to generate a graded, psychiatrically-loading over-withholding phenotype without any disorder-specific machinery. In REE terms this is the E3 commit threshold plus an urgency term, and the paper shows a single such parameter tracks a real symptom dimension.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two boundaries. (1) The threshold here governs WHEN TO STOP SAMPLING EXTERNAL EVIDENCE, not how deep to roll out an internal model -- REE's rollout_horizon and its commit threshold are different knobs, and this paper measures the analog of the latter. (2) The disorder assignment actively conflicts with MECH-080: extension-bias loads on compulsivity, not anxiety. Citing this as support for the claim as written would misreport what it found.
mapping.source_context: Human adolescents and young adults, NSPN population-representative cohort, dimensional psychiatric stratification rather than diagnosed groups; sequential information-gathering task with cost-free and costly sampling conditions.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality: large population-representative sample, dimensional rather than case-control design, explicit generative model. Mapping fidelity low because of the sampling-threshold vs rollout-depth substitution AND the arm misassignment. Transfer risk moderate: dimensional symptom scores to named disorders is itself a step.
